scenicChapters.title: Col de Turini
scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 74 km this is Col de Turini, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

nice-c-te-d-azur-col-de-turini-morning-a.story: Out of Olivetta San Michele, one way: 274 km, roughly 4 h 59 in the saddle. On the way it passes Saint-Étienne-de-Tinée, near Seillans and Saint-Laurent-du-Var. The climbs: Théoule-sur-Mer and Cap-d'Ail. It tops out at about 1,950 m. It crosses Italy, France and Monaco - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. Long stretches are under trees.

scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 17 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

places-abrigo-de-la-llagosa-abrigo-del-s.story: 71 km from Nerpio to Nerpio, about 1 h 13 of riding. It goes by way of Cueva del Gitano, Abrigo del Sabinar and back through Cueva del Gitano. The highest point is about 1,400 m. The line favours views over speed.

legend-halsema-highway.slogan: Halsema Highway – a named road, mapped from its own anchor points
legend-halsema-highway.story: A high mountain highway from Baguio, Luzon to Bontoc, Mountain Province, via Atok. Key character: Cordillera terraces; cloud forest; high ridges. Surface: paved and mixed.

scenicChapters.title: Halsema Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 23 km this is Halsema Highway, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.
